card.name: Candombe
card.era: Colonial era; Afro-Argentine presence in Buenos Aires from c. 1580; documented 18th-19th c.
card.tagline: Afro-Argentine drum-and-dance heritage of Buenos Aires barrios.
card.profile: Candombe is an Afro-Río de la Plata music-and-dance tradition. The Argentine (porteño) form, centered in Buenos Aires neighborhoods such as Monserrat, San Telmo, and La Boca, is played on two main hand drums - the 'llamador' (bass) and 'repicador' (sharp) - and danced by comparsas in street parades (llamadas) (English Wikipedia). The Argentine variety became largely private due to demographic decline and carnival bans, but is reviving in public street parades.
card.insight: Argentine candombe is a key root of milonga and tango and a living marker of Afro-Argentine identity; the Kikongo-derived word and the 'tangós' gathering places gave rise to the term tango (English Wikipedia; Buenos Aires City Government).
